editorial:
Road to Bali is the 1952 Hope/Crosby/Lamour entry in the Road series, directed by Hal Walker. The Internet Archive metadata describes it as two unemployed show-biz pals who take treasure-diving work in Bali for a local princess. Full-length copies run about 91 minutes, so a creator gets a complete feature to clip or screen.

The rights trap is that nobody has shown this film's copyright lapsed. Several Internet Archive uploads label it public domain for lack of renewal. That label comes from the uploaders and cites no renewal search. The renewal window runs 1979 to 1981, and the Stanford database could not be read in this session. Before reuse, search the Copyright Office public records and the Catalog of Copyright Entries yourself. Treat the film as protected until that search is done.
faq: Is Road to Bali in the public domain?

Not established. Internet Archive uploads claim a missing renewal, but no primary renewal search was confirmed here. Search the Stanford renewal database and the Copyright Office public records for renewals filed 1979 to 1981 before reusing it.
Can I use the Internet Archive copy?
Hosting on the Internet Archive is not a rights clearance. The public-domain mark on the item was added by the uploader. Rely on your own renewal search, not on the label.
